hints: Replace $\tan^2 x$ with $\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}$ in $3\tan^2 x - 3\sin^2 x - 4 = 0$.
Multiply the entire equation by $\cos^2 x$ to obtain $3\sin^2 x - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x - 4\cos^2 x = 0$.
Substitute $\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x$ into all occurrences of $\sin^2 x$ and collect powers of $\cos x$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the quotient identity $\tan^2 x = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}$ into the given equation:
$$3\left(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\right) - 3\sin^2 x - 4 = 0$$

Multiply every term by $\cos^2 x$ (for $\cos x \neq 0$):
$$3\sin^2 x - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x - 4\cos^2 x = 0$$

Replace $\sin^2 x$ with $1 - \cos^2 x$ using the Pythagorean identity:
$$3(1 - \cos^2 x) - 3(1 - \cos^2 x)\cos^2 x - 4\cos^2 x = 0$$

Expand and group powers of $\cos x$:
$$(3 - 3\cos^2 x) - (3\cos^2 x - 3\cos^4 x) - 4\cos^2 x = 0$$
$$3\cos^4 x - 10\cos^2 x + 3 = 0$$
where $a = 3$, $b = -10$, and $c = 3$.

hints: Treat $3\cos^4 x - 10\cos^2 x + 3 = 0$ as a quadratic in $\cos^2 x$ and factorise as $(3\cos^2 x - 1)(\cos^2 x - 3) = 0$.
walkthrough:
Factorise the quadratic in $\cos^2 x$ from part (a):
$$(3\cos^2 x - 1)(\cos^2 x - 3) = 0$$

Set each factor to zero:
$$\cos^2 x = 3 \quad (\text{no real solution as } -1 \le \cos x \le 1)$$
$$\cos^2 x = \frac{1}{3} \implies \cos x = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Find the angles in the range $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$:
$$\cos x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \implies x = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \approx 54.7^\circ$$
$$\cos x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \implies x = 180^\circ - 54.74^\circ \approx 125.3^\circ$$
